q.t: When current flows through a wire, a compass under it…
q.e: The current produces a magnetic field.

q.t: When the current stops, the magnetic field…
q.e: It vanishes the instant current stops.

q.t: Who discovered the magnetic effect of current in 1820?
q.e: Hans Christian Oersted, in Denmark.

q.t: A current-carrying coil that acts as a magnet is an…
q.e: Switch on: magnet; switch off: not.

q.t: Opposition to the flow of current is called…
q.e: Resistance turns some electrical energy into heat.

q.t: Heating elements are usually made of…
q.e: High resistance heats strongly.

q.t: Connecting wires in appliances are usually…
q.e: Low resistance so they stay cool.

q.t: Which uses the heating effect?
q.e: Also irons, heaters, hair dryers.

q.t: A dry cell's electrolyte is a…
q.e: Hence 'dry'.

q.t: Today's most common rechargeable battery is…
q.e: It depends on lithium and cobalt.

q.t: How does a compass show current is flowing?
o: Its needle (a tiny magnet) deflects in the field
q.e: Nothing else changed — only the current.

q.t: Why do most electromagnets have an iron core?
q.e: A coil with an iron nail picks up clips.

q.t: Which increases an electromagnet's strength?
q.e: Also more current and an iron core.

q.t: How do you reverse an electromagnet's poles?
q.e: Current direction decides polarity.

q.t: Why are lifting cranes fitted with electromagnets, not permanent magnets?
o: A permanent magnet could never let go
q.e: Switch off to release.

q.t: A compass's north pole is attracted to end A of an electromagnet. End A is…
q.e: Unlike poles attract.

q.t: Why does a nichrome wire heat up more than copper of the same size?
q.e: More resistance → more heat.

q.t: Outside a cell, current flows from…
q.e: Through the circuit from + to −.

q.t: In a lemon cell, the electrodes are…
q.e: Lemon juice is the electrolyte.

q.t: A 'dead' cell is one in which…
q.e: It can no longer supply electricity.

q.t: Volta replaced the frog's leg with salt-soaked paper and still got current. This showed electricity came from…
q.e: One substitution settled the dispute and led to the first battery.

q.t: What made Volta's test a good experiment?
q.e: Removing the frog alone, the effect survived.

q.t: Why must Oersted's result be repeated by others?
o: A result becomes accepted only when others can reproduce it
q.e: Reproducibility is key to science.

q.t: Why is the Earth a magnet?
o: Moving liquid iron in the core creates electric currents
q.e: Currents generate a field, as in a wire.

q.t: Why did dry cells replace Voltaic cells for daily use?
o: A paste can't spill, so cells can be sealed and carried
q.e: A glass jar of acid isn't portable.

q.t: Heat produced in a wire depends on…
o: Material, thickness, length, current and time
q.e: Two cells heat it more than one.

q.t: Why must wires and sockets be rated for the current?
o: Overheating can melt plastic and start fires
q.e: The heating effect can be a hazard.

q.t: Why do phone batteries need charging more often after a year or two?
o: They slowly wear out over charge cycles
q.e: Rechargeables don't last forever.

q.t: In the electromagnet activity, the wire ends also got warm. This shows…
o: Magnetic and heating effects happen together
q.e: The same current produced field and heat.

q.t: In a lemon cell chain, the LED doesn't glow. First try…
q.e: An LED conducts only with its longer wire to positive.

q.t: Three advantages of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet:
o: Switch on/off, adjust strength, reverse poles
q.e: All controlled electrically, with no moving parts.

q.t: An electromagnet with 1 cell lifts 3 clips. With 3 cells (same coil) it likely lifts…
q.e: More cells → more current → stronger field.

q.t: Which metal tends to act as the negative electrode with copper?
q.e: Copper is usually positive, zinc negative.

q.t: Galvani thought electricity came from…
q.e: Volta showed it came from metals + liquid.

q.t: Why is the heating effect a problem in transmission lines?
q.e: Energy is lost along the way.

q.t: A moving magnet can produce a current. This principle makes possible…
q.e: The link runs both ways.

q.t: Steel plants use electric furnaces to…
q.e: A large-scale use of the heating effect.

q.t: Why are solid-state batteries promising?
o: Safer, faster to charge and longer lasting
q.e: They replace liquid or paste electrolyte with a solid.

q.t: Which device uses the magnetic effect?
q.e: Bells, motors, fans, loudspeakers.

q.t: Migratory birds navigate using…
q.e: Earth's field also shields us from harmful space particles.
